name: Navistar S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Code Reference
source: Navistar Service Manual S08327 - Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes
usage_note: Curated retrieval index from the user-supplied 133-page Navistar service manual. Preserve SA + SPN + FMI together: the manual identifies the reporting module with Source Address and the failure mode with FMI. Vehicle configuration affects available source addresses and circuits. Use this source for the listed Navistar/International body-controller-era applications and do not silently generalize it to unrelated model years or architectures.

documents.title: Navistar S08327 body controller DTC application
documents.summary: S08327 is the Navistar Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes service-manual section dated August 16, 2010. It lists models 3200, 4100, 4300, 4400, 7300, 7400, 7500, 7600, 7700, 8500, 8600, BE 200, CE Bus, CXT, DuraStar, LoneStar, MXT, ProStar, RXT, TranStar and WorkStar.

documents.title: Displaying International/Navistar body-controller diagnostic codes
documents.summary: On non-VID vehicles equipped to display codes: set parking brake, use ACCESSORY for previously active codes or IGNITION for active plus previous codes, then momentarily press Cruise ON and Cruise Resume together. The cluster displays SPN, FMI, active/previous status, occurrence count (OC) and source address (SA). VID-equipped vehicles can display SPN, FMI, OC, SA and plain-text DTC descriptions when diagnostics are enabled/configured. Previously active DTCs require a service tool such as Diamond Logic Builder to clear; some may not clear by that method.

documents.title: Navistar S08327 FMI definitions
documents.summary: Manual definitions: FMI 0 above normal most severe; 1 below normal most severe; 2 erratic/intermittent/incorrect; 3 voltage above normal/short high; 4 voltage below normal/short low; 5 current below normal/open; 6 current above normal/grounded; 7 mechanical system not responding/out of adjustment; 8 abnormal frequency/pulse width/period; 9 abnormal update rate; 10 abnormal rate of change; 11 root cause unknown; 12 bad intelligent device/component; 13 out of calibration; 14 special instructions; 15 above normal least severe; 16 above normal moderately severe; 17 below normal least severe; 18 below normal moderately severe; 19 received network data in error; 20 drifted high; 21 drifted low; 31 condition exists.

documents.title: Navistar S08327 source addresses
documents.summary: S08327 source addresses include ECM 00, TCM 03, shift selector 05, ABS 11, electronic gauge cluster 23, compass 28, body controller 33, vehicle sensor module 39, VID 40, TPMS 51, rear HVAC 58, aftertreatment 61, telematics 74, AGSP3 132, secondary instrument cluster 167, HEV/Eaton transmission control pad 239, Power Pack 3 247, service tool 249 and global 255. Available addresses vary by vehicle configuration.

documents.title: International body controller J1939 and module communication faults
documents.summary: The manual contains numerous communication DTCs. Examples include SA23 SPN2000 FMI9 loss of data link from engine controller, SA23 SPN2003 FMI9 loss from transmission controller, SA23 SPN2011 FMI9 loss from ABS, and body-controller SA33 entries for engine/TCM/ABS/EGC/AGSP/rear-HVAC and other modules. SA33 SPN2000 FMI19 identifies PTC1 not received from engine with causes including ECM configuration/fault or drivetrain data link; SA33 SPN2003 FMI9 TCM communication failure; SA33 SPN2011 FMI9 ABS communication failure; SA33 SPN2023 FMI9 EGC communication failure. Diagnose reporting SA, expected module, power/ground and correct drivetrain/body-builder J1939 network before replacing a controller.

documents.title: International gauge cluster warning lamp and axle input DTCs
documents.summary: S08327 includes EGC/source-address 23 faults such as SPN171 FMI3/4 ambient-air-temperature analog input high/low, SPN623 FMI5 red stop lamp open/low current, SPN624 FMI5 amber warning lamp, SPN987 FMI5 protect lamp, SPN1213 FMI5 MIL, SPN1438 FMI5 ABS/EBS amber lamp, SPN1439 FMI5 EBS red lamp, SPN1725 FMI3/4 front axle pressure analog input, SPN1727 FMI3/4 rear axle pressure, SPN1792 FMI5 tractor-mounted trailer ABS warning and SPN1793 FMI5 ATC/ASR warning.

documents.title: International body-controller switches relay drivers and configuration faults
documents.summary: The body-controller list includes configuration-aware switch-pack and relay-driver faults. FMI13 entries can mean an unexpected switch/load exists on a position configured as empty/unused, directing diagnosis toward configuration plus harness/switch state rather than automatic component replacement. Examples include SPN520915-520920 relay-driver channels and SPN520840-520863/520922-520927 switch-pack positions. SPN520929-520934 cover AGSP switch locations; SPN520935-520936 cluster switch locations.

documents.title: International body controller output circuit DTC patterns
documents.summary: S08327 repeatedly uses FMI5 for under-current/open-circuit output faults and FMI6 for over-current/grounded or short-to-ground faults. Examples near the end of the manual include SPN520928 DRL tell-tale relay command, SPN520937 TSS module power control, SPN520939 air-brake-pressure indicator relay driver, SPN520940 power-adjustable-pedals enable relay and SPN520941 Hydromax pump motor relay driver.

documents.title: International/Navistar rear HVAC diagnostic trouble codes
documents.summary: Rear HVAC source address 58 includes SPN109 FMI14 high refrigerant pressure/sensor issue, SPN168 FMI3 battery voltage above 16 VDC and FMI4 below 12.1 VDC, SPN1547 duct-inlet/evaporator temperature conditions, SPN1548 HVAC duct-temperature sensor voltage faults, SPN2058 FMI9 communication failure, SPN520210 blower output voltage/short faults, SPN520211 FMI7 actuator position not responding, SPN520212 dimmer output high/low, SPN520213 evaporator sensor high/low and no-idle relay/datalink faults SPN520808-520812.

documents.title: Panta rule for Navistar S08327 diagnosis
documents.summary: For S08327 faults, identify the complete SA + SPN + FMI and whether active or previously active. SA identifies the reporting module; SPN identifies the diagnosed item; FMI identifies the detected failure type; OC is occurrence count. Preserve model/configuration context because circuits, modules and source addresses vary. Use the manual's cause/comments/pin/logical-signal fields when available, and do not convert a DTC into an automatic parts-replacement recommendation.
